newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN DLR ENDS SHARPLY DOWN ON U.S. DLR STRENGTH.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN DLR ENDS SHARPLY DOWN ON U.S. DLR STRENGTH.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed sharply lower against its U.S. counterpart on Friday as the greenback's worldwide strength triggered hectic buying despite the central bank's show of defence on Thursday, dealers said.
The local unit ended at T$28.739 against Thursday's T$28.639 close.
Turnover through dealers was active at US$344 million.
Dealers said the central bank's late Thursday intervention did not dampen greenback buying on Friday.

"As you can see, the underlying demand for the U.S. dollar remains very strong," said one dealer at a foreign bank. "The market knows the central bank does not like volatility, but it does not oppose a slow depreciation," the dealer said.
Dealers had said the central bank's move was a clear attempt to rein in offshore speculators, who had been buying U.S. dollars in the form of non-delivery forward trading.
Friday's greenback demand came from at both domestic and abroad, dealers said.

"Most people feel it's unlikely for the Taiwan dollar to return to above T$28 in the immediate future. Who knows when it will hit T$29 or T$30 -- that's why the U.S. dollar demand is so heavy," the dealer said.
A range of T$28.70-80 was seen for Saturday.
